alloy.preparation: F1 model stainless steel from 50 kg vacuum-melted ingot, rolled to 1–1.5 mm sheet with intermediate annealing and pickling. Numerical anneal temperature/time not supplied. Specimens for Ep measurement polished to 600-grit finish; electrode dimensions and any individual subsequent degreasing are not restated. The 320-grit acetone-degreased immersion/crevice coupons are described separately.

test_solution.preparation: Argon-deaerated 3.5% NaCl; gas duration, solvent grade, percentage basis and numerical pH are not supplied for this Ep test.

test_method.procedure_description: Potentiostat anodic polarization at 20 mV/min in 3.5% NaCl at 80 °C; Figure 2 potentials on Ag/AgCl scale. Reference filling solution, counter details, starting potential and hold schedule are not independently specified. Figure 2 alloy labels identify the Table 1 row; Cr+3Mo index is not used to calculate missing chemistry. The 60 °C crevice-repassivation step sequence and low-pH/high-chloride curves are separate methods.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Ep is the potential where polarizing current exceeded 10 µA/cm² and continued increasing without oscillation. Plotted bar endpoints retain the source presentation; their statistical meaning is not specified.

experiments.result_note: Ep criterion: current exceeds 10 μA/cm² and continues increasing without oscillation. Visible bar endpoints retained; their statistical meaning is not specified. Table 1 actual mass% chemistry retained; F1 Mo strictly <0.003 mass%. No Fe balance, NaCl percentage conversion or chloride molarity is calculated. Acid adjustment with HCl belongs to other anodic-curve solutions and is not added to Figure 2. FeCl3/HCl immersion, boiling H2SO4 and crevice repassivation protocols do not replace this 80 °C Ep method.
